title: Chapter 33. Nagari Padas — VII: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 169–180; sects. 2.4, 3.1, 5.1, 5.2): the quarrels of the heavenly women, the townswomen's words at the Lord's wedding; concluding note
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.

1. Narahari — "brajapure rasabilāsa biśeṣa…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 169; GCC 10.25)

Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The heavenly woman who closed the dispute (chapter 32, no. 23) tells her friend in confidence: who can tell the special plays of rasa in Vraja? Yet He is the very same, and with all the same dear companions He ever sports in Nadia, absorbed in singing of His own virtues; first giving His own the nectar of His beauty to drink, He made them as if mad, and the young noble wives, bidding farewell to family and shame, made Gora their very essence. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 10, pada 25.1

ব্রজপুরে রসবিলাস বিশেষ সে সকল কেবা কহিতে পারে ।
গুপতে রাখিহ দিহ চিত যাহা কহিয়া আপনা জানিয়া তোরে ॥

brajapure rasabilāsa biśeṣa se sakala kebā kahite pāre |
gupate rākhiha diha cita yāhā kahiyā āpanā jāniyā tore ||

brajapure — in the city of Vraja; rasabilāsa biśeṣa — the special plays of rasa; se sakala kebā kahite pāre — who can tell them all; gupate rākhiha — keep it secret; diha cita — attend (lit. "give the mind"); yāhā kahiyā — to what I shall say; āpanā jāniyā tore — counting you as my own

1.1"The special plays of rasa in the city of Vraja — who can tell them all? Keep it secret; attend to what I tell you, counting you as my own.

এই সেই সেই এই সেই সব প্রিয়পরিকর সঙ্গেতে লৈয়া ।
বিহরয়ে সদা নদীয়ানগরে নিজ গুণগানে মগন হৈয়া ॥

ei sei sei ei sei saba priyaparikara saṅgete laiyā |
biharaye sadā nadīyānagare nija guṇagāne magana haiyā ||

ei sei sei ei — this is He, He is this; sei saba priya-parikara — all the same dear companions; saṅgete laiyā — taking along; biharaye sadā — ever sports; nadīyā-nagare — in the city of Nadia; nija guṇagāne — in singing of His own virtues; magana haiyā — absorbed

1.2This is He, and He is this: taking with Him all the same dear companions, He ever sports in the city of Nadia, absorbed in singing of His own virtues.

অপরূপ রূপমাধুরী অমিয়া পিয়াইয়া আগে আপন জনে ।
উনমত মত মতি গতি করু তাহে তারা কেহ কিছু না গণে ॥

aparūpa rūpamādhurī amiyā piyāiyā āge āpana jane |
unamata mata mati gati karu tāhe tārā keha kichu nā gaṇe ||

aparūpa rūpa-mādhurī amiyā — the nectar of the wondrous sweetness of form; piyāiyā āge — first giving to drink; āpana jane — to His own; unamata mata — as if mad; mati gati karu — made their minds and steps; tāhe tārā keha kichu nā gaṇe — and they count nothing

1.3First giving His own the nectar of the wondrous sweetness of His form to drink, He made their minds and their steps as if mad — and they count nothing else.

নব নব কুলবতী কুল কুল-কলঙ্ক লাজে তিলাঞ্জলি দিয়া ।
নরহরি সাথী সার কৈল সবে সুখময় গোরা পরাণপিয়া ॥

naba naba kulabatī kula kula-kalaṅka lāje tilāñjali diyā |
narahari sāthī sāra kaila sabe sukhamaya gorā parāṇapiyā ||

naba naba kulabatī — ever new noble wives; kula kula-kalaṅka lāje — to family, family disgrace and shame; tilāñjali diyā — giving the last libation; narahari sāthī — Narahari the witness; sāra kaila sabe — all made their essence; sukhamaya gorā — Gora full of joy; parāṇapiyā — the Beloved of their life

1.4Ever new noble wives, giving the last libation to family, to the family's disgrace and to shame, have all made their essence Gora, full of joy, the Beloved of their life — Narahari is witness to it."2

GCC — kirana 10, pada 25 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135), "yathārāga". Who speaks. The tenth kirana of GCC is the morning talk of the heavenly women (debaramaṇī) looking down on Nadia from the sky (chapter 32, note 24); padas 10.25–10.26 (nos. 1–2 of this chapter) close their talk: one tells another "in confidence", and the other asks to be taught how to come and live in Nadia. GCC readings: "gupate rākhiyā dio cita yāhā kahiye āpana jāniyā tore" ("keeping it secret, attend…"), "nija guṇagaṇe" ("absorbed in His own virtues"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). teaching of the tradition (CC, Adi 1 and 3–4; Kavi Karnapura's "Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika" names who among Gaura's companions was whom in Vraja). But the gopis in Gaura-lila are not townswomen of Nadia in love with Gaura: the Lord Himself came in Radha's bhava to taste Her love (CC, Adi 4), and therefore the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the speaker's conclusion — that "the young wives of Nadia made Gora, as a nagara, their essence" (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the original. "Absorbed in singing of His own virtues" — cf. CB, Madhya (the Lord in bhavavesha sings of Himself). "To give the last libation" (tilāñjali) — to abandon for good.

2. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 170; GCC 10.26)

Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The listener, hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, is filled with joy and cannot hold back tears of love; joining her palms, she asks to be taught how she might once come to live in Nadia and be a companion of its young playful women, keep Narahari's Beloved in her heart and be rid of the cruel barrier. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 10, pada 26.3

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের সুচারু চরিত শুনি শুনি ধনী পরমসুখী ।
ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে বারে বারে প্রেমনীরে ভরে যুগল আঁখি ॥

gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita śuni śuni dhanī paramasukhī |
dhairaja dharite nāre bāre bāre premanīre bhare yugala ām̐khi ||

gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita — of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds; śuni śuni — hearing and hearing; dhanī parama-sukhī — the fair one, filled with joy; dhairaja dharite nāre — cannot hold her composure; bāre bāre — again and again; prema-nīre bhare yugala ām̐khi — both eyes fill with tears of love

2.1Hearing and hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, the fair one was filled with joy; she cannot hold her composure — again and again both eyes fill with tears of love.

যুড়ি করে কর করিয়া প্রণাম কহে পুনঃ মৃদু মধুর কথা ।
নিজ জন জানি এত দিনে যেন ঘুচাইলে সব হিয়ার ব্যথা ॥

yuṛi kare kara kariyā praṇāma kahe punaḥ mṛdu madhura kathā |
nija jana jāni eta dine yena ghucāile saba hiyāra byathā ||

yuṛi kare kara — joining hand to hand; kariyā praṇāma — bowing; kahe punaḥ mṛdu madhura kathā — again speaks soft, sweet words; nija jana jāni — counting me your own; eta dine — at last; yena — as it were; ghucāile saba hiyāra byathā — you have removed all the pain of the heart

2.2Joining her palms and bowing, she again speaks soft, sweet words: "Counting me as your own, at last you have, as it were, taken all the pain from my heart.

নিবেদিয়ে এই নদীয়ানগরে বারেক বসতি কিরূপে পাব ।
আর নব নব রঙ্গিণীগণের সঙ্গিনী হইয়া কিরূপে রব ॥

nibediye ei nadīyānagare bāreka basati kirūpe pāba |
āra naba naba raṅgiṇīgaṇera saṅginī haiyā kirūpe raba ||

nibediye — I pray; ei nadīyā-nagare — in this city of Nadia; bāreka basati kirūpe pāba — how might I once find a dwelling; āra — and; naba naba raṅgiṇīgaṇa — of the ever new playful beauties; saṅginī haiyā — becoming a companion; kirūpe raba — how might I live

2.3I pray: how might I once dwell in this city of Nadia? And how might I live as a companion of these ever new playful beauties?

নরহরি-প্রাণপিয়া হিয়া মাঝে রাখিয়া ঘুচাব দারুণ বাধা ।
কহ কহ ওগো উপায় কিরূপে সফল হবে এ সকল সাধা ॥

narahari-prāṇapiyā hiyā mājhe rākhiyā ghucāba dāruṇa bādhā |
kaha kaha ogo upāya kirūpe saphala habe e sakala sādhā ||

narahari-prāṇapiyā — the Beloved of Narahari's life; hiyā mājhe rākhiyā — keeping within the heart; ghucāba dāruṇa bādhā — I shall remove the cruel barrier; kaha kaha ogo — tell, tell; upāya kirūpe — by what means; saphala habe — will be fulfilled; e sakala sādhā — all these wishes

2.4Keeping the Beloved of Narahari's life within my heart, I shall be rid of the cruel barrier. Tell me, tell me: by what means will all these wishes be fulfilled?"

(catalogue: NG-362). GCC — kirana 10, pada 26 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135). 2.4 "be fulfilled" follows GPT2 and GCC "saphala" (GPT1 "sakala", a misprint); "barrier" — GPT1 and GCC "bādhā" (GPT2 "dhām̐dhā", "bewilderment"). The wish of heavenly beings to be born where the Lord reveals His lila is a commonplace of the hagiographies (CB, Adi: the gods long to be born in Navadvipa to share in the Lord's sankirtana); the "cruel barrier" is that one living in the city of the gods cannot come to Nadia. The closing pada of the kirana (GCC 10.27) is not in GPT: the fair one told her friend all she had asked, and the heavenly women, trembling and winking at one another, gave themselves to merry play, gazing at Narahari's Lord; the colophon: "the description of the play of the heavenly women filled with love for Him". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

3. Narahari — "surapura mājhe basati kariyā…" (GPT1 pp. 233–234, no. 171; GCC 11.4)

An answer: defence of the chastity of the women of Nadia (the heavenly women's talk; by content not nagari-bhava). The opening of the eleventh kirana of GCC — "the love-quarrels of the heavenly women". A heavenly woman who has just arrived angrily rebukes her friends: living in the city of the gods, they have grown proud and slander the women of Nadia; what they describe happens only with the young wives of Vraja, while the wives of Nadia are faithful to their husbands, do not see another man's face even in a dream, revere their elders; whoever sings of others' disgrace is disgraced. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 11, pada 4.4

সুরপুর মাঝে বসতি করিয়া এত অহঙ্কার করিছ কেনে ।
নদীয়ার নারীগণে পরিবাদ দিতে ভয় কিছু না হয় মনে ॥

surapura mājhe basati kariyā eta ahaṅkāra karicha kene |
nadīyāra nārīgaṇe paribāda dite bhaya kichu nā haya mane ||

surapura mājhe basati kariyā — dwelling in the city of the gods; eta ahaṅkāra karicha kene — why such pride; nadīyāra nārīgaṇe — the women of Nadia; paribāda dite — to slander; bhaya kichu nā haya mane — you feel no fear at heart

3.1"Living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud? You feel no fear at heart in slandering the women of Nadia!

হায় হায় হেন বিপরীত বাণী শুনিয়া কি আমি সহিতে পারি ।
না জানিয়ে তোমা সবার কি দোষ করিলে এ সব নদ্যার নারী ॥

hāya hāya hena biparīta bāṇī śuniyā ki āmi sahite pāri |
nā jāniye tomā sabāra ki doṣa karile e saba nadyāra nārī ||

hāya hāya — alas, alas; hena biparīta bāṇī śuniyā — hearing such perverse words; ki āmi sahite pāri — can I bear it; nā jāniye — I do not know; tomā sabāra ki doṣa karile — what wrong they did to you all; e saba nadyāra nārī — these women of Nadia

3.2Alas, alas! Hearing such perverse words, how can I bear it? I do not know what wrong these women of Nadia have done to you all.

নিজ নিজ রীতিমত জান আনে না জান আনের মরম কথা ।
না বুঝহ কিছু কিসে কিবা হয় তেঁই বলি দেহ ধরিলে বৃথা ॥

nija nija rītimata jāna āne nā jāna ānera marama kathā |
nā bujhaha kichu kise kibā haya tem̐i bali deha dharile bṛthā ||

nija nija rītimata — by your own ways; jāna āne — you judge others; nā jāna ānera marama kathā — you do not know others' heart; nā bujhaha kichu — you understand nothing; kise kibā haya — what comes of what; tem̐i bali — so I say; deha dharile bṛthā — in vain you bear a body

3.3You judge others by your own ways and do not know the secret of others' hearts; you understand nothing — what comes of what; so I say: in vain do you bear a body.

যেরূপ কহ সে সম্ভব কেবল ব্রজপুরে নব রমণীগণে ।
নদীয়ার যত যুবতী অতি সুপতিব্রতা জানে জগত জনে ॥

yerūpa kaha se sambhaba kebala brajapure naba ramaṇīgaṇe |
nadīyāra yata yubatī ati supatibratā jāne jagata jane ||

yerūpa kaha — what you describe; se sambhaba kebala — is possible only; brajapure naba ramaṇīgaṇe — with the young wives in the city of Vraja; nadīyāra yata yubatī — all the young wives of Nadia; ati supatibratā — most faithful to their husbands; jāne jagata jane — the people of the world know

3.4What you describe is possible only with the young wives in the city of Vraja; but all the young wives of Nadia are the most faithful of the faithful — the whole world knows it.

পরপতি মুখ না দেখে স্বপনে না চলে কভু কুপথ দিয়া ।
না জানে চাতুরি কপট শঠতা সতত সবার সরল হিয়া ॥

parapati mukha nā dekhe svapane nā cale kabhu kupatha diyā |
nā jāne cāturi kapaṭa śaṭhatā satata sabāra sarala hiyā ||

parapati mukha — another husband's face; nā dekhe svapane — they do not see even in a dream; nā cale kabhu kupatha diyā — never walk an evil road; nā jāne cāturi kapaṭa śaṭhatā — know no tricks, deceit, guile; satata sabāra sarala hiyā — the hearts of all ever simple

3.5They do not see another husband's face even in a dream, never walk an evil road; they know no tricks, no deceit, no guile — all of them always simple of heart.

ধৈর্য্যবতী কার্য্যে বিচক্ষণা চারু প্রবৃত্তি পরম ধরম পথে ।
অতুলিত কুল লাজ ভয় কভু ভুলি না বৈসয়ে কুজন সাথে ॥

dhairyyabatī kāryye bicakṣaṇā cāru prabṛtti parama dharama pathe |
atulita kula lāja bhaya kabhu bhuli nā baisaye kujana sāthe ||

dhairyabatī — steadfast; kārye bicakṣaṇā — skilful in work; cāru prabṛtti — of lovely conduct; parama dharama pathe — on the highest path of dharma; atulita kula lāja bhaya — the matchless family shame and fear; kabhu bhuli — ever, forgetting; nā baisaye kujana sāthe — they do not sit with a bad man

3.6Steadfast, skilful in their work, of lovely conduct — always on the highest path of dharma; mindful of the matchless shame of family and of fear, never, forgetting themselves, do they sit with a bad man.

গুরুজন প্রাণসম বাসে সবে শুভ রাশি গুণ গণিতে নারি ।
মোর মনে এই এ সবারে সদা আঁখি মাঝে রাখি যতন করি ॥

gurujana prāṇasama bāse sabe śubha rāśi guṇa gaṇite nāri |
mora mane ei e sabāre sadā ām̐khi mājhe rākhi yatana kari ||

gurujana prāṇasama bāse sabe — all love their elders as life; śubha rāśi guṇa gaṇite nāri — their host of good virtues I cannot count; mora mane ei — in my heart this; e sabāre sadā — them all always; ām̐khi mājhe rākhi — to keep in my eyes; yatana kari — with care

3.7They all love their elders as their life; their auspicious virtues cannot be counted. In my heart there is one thing: always to keep them with care in my eyes.

তাহে কহি সহবাসী জানি বাণী মানিবে নিশ্চয় না কহি আনে ।
পরের কলঙ্ক গায় যেই সেই কলঙ্কী এ নরহরি তা জানে ॥

tāhe kahi sahabāsī jāni bāṇī mānibe niścaya nā kahi āne |
parera kalaṅka gāya yei sei kalaṅkī e narahari tā jāne ||

tāhe kahi — so I say; sahabāsī jāni — knowing you are neighbours; bāṇī mānibe niścaya — you will surely accept the words; nā kahi āne — I say nothing else; parera kalaṅka gāya yei — whoever sings another's disgrace; sei kalaṅkī — is disgraced; e narahari tā jāne — this Narahari knows

3.8So I tell you: knowing that you are my neighbours, you will surely accept these words — I say nothing else. Whoever sings of another's disgrace is herself disgraced: this Narahari knows."5

scan PDF pp. 137–138), "yathārāga". Who speaks. The eleventh kirana of GCC is headed "Again in the morning — the love-quarrels and so on of the heavenly women"; its opening is not in GPT: from the sky the heavenly women drink the nectar of Gaura's form as He plays in Shachi's courtyard and argue — some say that the nagaris of Nadia "have gone mad for the Beloved" and will bring disgrace on themselves, others answer that the wives of Vraja did the same (GCC 11.1); a short pada on the heavenly women's rapture (11.2); praise of the love of Nadia's young wives — and then "a heavenly woman arrived and, waving her hand, said angrily to all" (11.3). GCC readings: "nā jāniyā" (3.2), "tem̐i bali" (3.3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27); this pada answers it. of Nadia are faithful wives. Gaudiya theology agrees: the parakiya-rasa of the gopis belongs to Vraja (CC, Adi 4), and in Navadvipa the Lord did not accept the worship of women as a nagara (CB, Adi). The pada is therefore by content not nagari-bhava (like nos. 19–20 of chapter 32); in the heavenly women's dispute, however, her words will be mocked (nos. 4–10). "Neighbours" (sahabāsī, 3.8) — those who live with her in the city of the gods.

4. Narahari — "bhāla bhāla ihā śikhāte habe nā…" (GPT1 p. 234, no. 172; GCC 11.6)

Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). A mocker answers the defender: they need no teaching — as if they did not know: on earth only the wives of Nadia are faithful, and in the city of the gods only she; they themselves, forever singing of others' disgrace, will be disgraced, but will not make her a sharer; how can so clever a woman live among the unchaste? Let her go to Nadia with her dharma and her shame and live among the chaste. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 11, pada 6.6

ভাল ভাল ইহা শিখাতে হবে না এ সকল কথা না জানি এ আমি ।
অবনীতে নৈদা নারী পতিব্রতা সুরপুর মাঝে কেবল তুমি ॥

bhāla bhāla ihā śikhāte habe nā e sakala kathā nā jāni e āmi |
abanīte naidā nārī patibratā surapura mājhe kebala tumi ||

bhāla bhāla — well, well; ihā śikhāte habe nā — no need to teach this; e sakala kathā nā jāni e āmi — as if I did not know all this; abanīte — on earth; naidā nārī patibratā — the wives of Nadia are faithful; surapura mājhe kebala tumi — in the city of the gods only you

4.1"Well, well! No need to teach us this — as if I did not know it all! On earth only the wives of Nadia are faithful to their husbands, and in the city of the gods only you!

অনুখন পর কলঙ্ক গাইয়া কলঙ্কিনী মোরা সকলে হব ।

Summary of chapter 33

The chapter completes the padas signed "Narahari" in nagari-bhava. All 20 padas are "probably Chakravarti" (B). GPT1 3.2 nos. 169–180 (nos. 1–12) = GCC 10.25–10.26 and the eleventh kirana of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" ("the love-quarrels of the heavenly women"): 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.15, 11.17 and 11.14 — GPT rearranged the padas (no. 177 = 11.15, no. 178 = 11.17) and split 11.14 into two (nos. 179–180). The speakers are heavenly women looking down on Nadia from the sky: one defends the chastity of the women of Nadia (no. 3 — by content not nagari-bhava), the others mock her, tell of the townswomen's "pranks" and call Narahari's Lord "the husband of them all" (no. 10) — yet they themselves describe the Lord as strict: He does not raise His face, turns away, hurries home in shame (nos. 5, 7, 8, 12). GPT padas outside section 3.2: 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21 (nos. 13–16) — the women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding with Vishnupriya (a dream with an embrace, setting out for Shachi's house, "Madana's arrow", wishes to touch His body; all in the twelfth wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara", no. 7 also in GCC 9.22); 3.1 nos. 129–130 (nos. 17–18) — found in GCC (10.8–10.9, the heavenly women's words on Gaura's morning appearance; no. 130 was not in the catalogue — new line NG-366; for no. 129, NG-248, "Sarakara?, no witnesses" is replaced by B); 5.1 no. 12 (no. 19, jhulana) and 5.2 no. 39 (no. 20, a walk through the town) — in BR. Where GCC or BR is more outspoken than GPT (no. 8 — an extra couplet in GCC; no. 16 — BR's "bridal chamber"), GPT is translated; the only place where GPT is more outspoken than GCC is the last couplet of no. 12 ("the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara" instead of GCC's words that Narahari preserved propriety; note 20). The open motifs of attraction and sambhoga (nos. 7, 10, 13, 15, 16) are rendered exactly, with notes on the tradition's position.

Concluding note on the "Narahari" nagari padas (chapters 29–33)

1. How many. In the section of nagari padas, 102 padas signed "Narahari" from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini" have been translated: chapter 29 — 15 (Narahari Chakravarti's pada NG-079 from the cycle of the twelfth wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara"; GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45; nos. 86–93), chapter 30 — 21 (nos. 94–110, 120–123), chapter 31 — 23 (nos. 119, 124–145), chapter 32 — 23 (nos. 146–168), chapter 33 — 20 (nos. 169–180; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21; 3.1 nos. 129–130; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). Of the 95 padas signed Narahari in section 3.2 of GPT, 94 are translated here — all except no. 41 (= PK 103 of Narahari Sarakara, translated in the main part, chapter 3); the other 8 are nagari padas from sections 2.4, 3.1, 5.1, 5.2. No. 119 (Gaura in sleep speaks Krishna's words) is by content not nagari-bhava, as are the rebuttals within the heavenly women's dispute (chapter 32, nos. 19–20; chapter 33, no. 3).

2. Attribution. "Probably Chakravarti" (B) — 81 padas: 75 are found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" (GCC, ed. 1947) — padas 2.13; 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16, 7.29–7.30; 8.2–8.20; 9.1–9.2, 9.6–9.16, 9.22; 10.8–10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26; 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14 (two padas in GPT), 11.15, 11.17 — and 6 occur only in the "Bhakti-ratnakara" (NG-079; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 21; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). "Not established" or "probably Sarakara" (C) — 21 padas: six short padas GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45 in plain Bengali (the GPT2 index assigns them to Sarakara; there are no other witnesses; no. 43 — "not established") and fifteen padas nos. 100–110, 120–123, which stand in GPT in the place of the lost pages of the only available scan of GCC (pp. 81–88 = GCC 7.17–7.28; apparently also from GCC). Not one "Narahari" nagari pada of GPT is confirmed by PK or by other early collections as a song of Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's companion; almost all of them are Narahari Chakravarti's poetic elaboration of the nagari motif (first half of the 18th century). The collation confirms Majumdar's argument: the long padas of GPT with this signature do not belong to Sarakara.

3. The composition of GCC 7–11 in GPT. Kiranas 7–11 of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" describe morning in Navadvipa: the townswomen of Nadia talk of Gaura and of how, deceiving their strict elders, they saw Him (kirana 7), tell their dreams (8), go to Shachi's house and dream of meeting Him (9); then the heavenly women look down on Nadia from the sky — praise its nagaris, argue about Gaura (10) and quarrel among themselves (11). These five kiranas have 121 padas (12 of them on the lost pages of the scan); the compiler of GPT took at least 78 and distributed them among his sections: — kirana 7: 7.1 — in sect. 2.2 (GPT1 p. 68, no. 19; chapter 19); 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16 = 3.2 nos. 86–99 (no. 97 is only the second half of 7.14); 7.29–7.30 = nos. 124–125; not taken: 7.13 and the closing 7.31; 7.17–7.28 are lost in the scan (in their place — nos. 100–110, 120–123); — kirana 8: 8.2–8.20 = nos. 126–144; not taken: the opening 8.1 and the closing 8.21; — kirana 9: 9.1–9.2 = nos. 145–146; 9.6–9.16 = nos. 147–157 (9.12 = no. 150 stands earlier in GPT); 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22 — in sect. 2.4 ("the second marriage", nos. 4–7: where they also stand in BR's wedding narrative); not taken: 9.3–9.5, 9.17, 9.20 and the closing prayer 9.23; — kirana 10: 10.7 — GPT1 p. 494, no. 30 (chapter 18, no. 28); 10.8–10.9 — in sect. 3.1, "form" (nos. 129–130); 10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26 = 3.2 nos. 158–170; not taken: the opening 10.1–10.6, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 and the closing 10.27; — kirana 11: 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14, 11.15, 11.17 = nos. 171–180 (in a different order; 11.14 split into nos. 179–180); not taken: the opening 11.1–11.3, the links 11.5, 11.16, the padas 11.11–11.13 and the close 11.18–11.19. Besides these, GCC 2.13 (Gaura's words in sleep) stands in GPT 3.2 (no. 119).

4. Who speaks. In GCC the padas of kiranas 7–9 are the words of the townswomen of Nadia (and of a mother-in-law who sends her daughters-in-law to Shachi, 9.2); the padas of kiranas 10–11 are the words of heavenly women (debaramaṇī), who only watch Nadia from the sky and long to be born there. In GPT the openings, colophons and links of the kiranas are left out, and all the padas of section 3.2 read as the words of townswomen; but traces remain in the GPT text itself — "you, connoisseurs of rasa in the city of the gods", "in the city of the gods a rumour has arisen", "living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud", "how will you live alone in the city of the gods" (chapter 32, nos. 17, 20; chapter 33, nos. 3, 4, 10). Therefore 25 padas of GPT (3.2 nos. 158–180 and 3.1 nos. 129–130) are translated with the label "the heavenly women's talk".

5. Where GPT softens GCC. The compiler of GPT did not take the most outspoken padas (10.11 — one heavenly woman's guess at where Gaura spent the night; 11.11–11.13 — the antics of women at the ghat and on the road), left out single lines (8.15; the couplet in 11.10 about a shadow touching Gora's body) and replaced single words (8.6 "lay down" → "sat"; 8.11, 8.14, 8.16 — mentions of Madana, e.g. 8.14 "rapt with Madana" → "rapt with joy"; 8.18 — "breast"; 9.6 — "under Madana's weight"; 9.13 "the cloth over the breast" → "the cloth over the face"; 9.14 "wants to embrace" → "wants to see your dear face"). Throughout, GPT's text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR and in the notes. The reverse case occurs once: the last couplet of no. 180 (chapter 33, no. 12), where in place of GCC's words that Narahari, being with Gauranga, preserved propriety stands the formula "in Nadia the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass"; the compiler's work is also the signature "Narahari" at the end of no. 179, where GCC has no poet's name.

6. Conclusion. The "Narahari" nagari padas of GPT are not songs of a contemporary of the Lord but a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the nagari motif, carried over from the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and the "Bhakti-ratnakara" into an anthology of the early 20th century, abridged and without the author's frame. Within that frame Narahari Chakravarti himself never shows Gaura responding to the women's attraction: the Lord passes by without raising His face, turns away, hurries home, performs expiation, and His companion leads Him away (GCC 11.11–11.14; chapter 32, nos. 19–20; chapter 33, nos. 5, 7, 8, 12); the wishes and dreams are the heroines' imagining, and in kiranas 10–11 it is even a dispute of heavenly women about what they have not seen. Everything is translated faithfully to the author — without worldly vocabulary beyond the original and without softening — with notes on the tradition's position: Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati do not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari"; Gaura is Krishna Himself in Radha's bhava and radiance, tasting Her love as a devotee, not as the enjoyer (introductory note, chapter 27). What remains of the section is the padas of Lochana Dasa from GPT 3.2 (nos. 61–85, 116; chapter 34) and the concluding note to the whole section of nagari padas.
